Subject: Renewal planning — pricing pressure and next steps

Rishi,

We are kicking off renewal discussions for our enterprise account (term ends Aug 31). We've seen notice from a couple of vendors about pricing resets in H2, and leadership asked us to explore any options to lock rates or reduce exposure.

High-level asks from procurement:
- Can Redwood offer a price lock via multi-year prepay (1–3yr) that avoids an annual rate increase?
- We need flexibility for usage swings (+/- 30% year over year) without punitive true-up charges.
- Any escrow-like protections if performance targets aren’t met (SLOs)?

Appreciate a sketch of viable structures and a quick call — Sara (procurement) is on copy. Ideally we have a strawman by end of week.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director of Platform Engineering
OliveAI

Subject: Re: Renewal planning — pricing pressure and next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear ask. Quick overview of three structures that map to your goals; I'll attach a more detailed workbook and a proposed MAP.

1) Anchored multi-year prepay (recommended)
   - 2 or 3 year prepay that sets unit price for AI inference at today’s rate (lock).
   - Annual true-up window with a +/-30% swing band: if usage within band, no reconciliation; outside band triggers a netting true-up at a mid-tier rate.
   - Performance escrow: a small portion (3–5%) of prepaid dollars held in escrow and released quarterly conditioned on meeting latency/error SLOs.

2) Phased prepay with kicker credits
   - Year 1 partial prepay + Years 2–3 options; if growth exceeds forecast, customer receives extra committed credits (kicker) to offset marginal usage.

3) Capacity reservation + on-demand overlay
   - Reserve baseline capacity (guaranteed throughput) at a discount; on-demand tokens billed at list but with monthly smoothing. Lower price certainty but more flexible.

Key tradeoffs: longer prepays give deeper discounts but reduce flexibility; escrow protects you but adds accounting steps.

Next steps: Ben will run a committable pricing table with numbers; Laura can own the MAP and legal kickoff; Monica will scope operational SLO wording for the escrow. Can we do a 30-minute sync Thu 4/22?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

- True-up timing: we request semi-annual true-ups instead of annual to reduce exposure.
- Migration/region risk: if Redwood needs to move instances across regions for capacity, what guarantees on latency/locality?

Also please include a sample contract clause for the escrow release triggers and the proposed SLOs. We'll have legal glance it before the sync.

Subject: Pricing strawman for OliveAI — anchored prepay + semi-annual true-up

Sara/Jordan — attaching the numbers file (Redwood_Prepay_Structures_v3.xlsx). Executive summary below.

Strawman (2-year anchored prepay):
- Total prepay: $1.2M over 24 months (paid up front)
- Effective unit discount vs list: 18%
- Swing band: +/-30% per year; semi-annual reconciliation at 6-month cadence (customer-friendly)
- Escrow: 4% of prepay held in a refundable account; released quarterly upon meeting SLOs (latency p95 < 220ms; error rate < 0.5%).
- Kicker: if YOY usage growth > 40% and customer paid full prepay for Year 2, Redwood issues one-time bonus credits equal to 5% of overage.

Alternative (phased 3-yr): lower upfront ($600k yr1), step-up credits, lower immediate cash burden but smaller discount (12%).

Open items for legal: escrow custody instructions, definition of SLO measurement window, dispute resolution for metric disagreements.

Can we lock the 4/22 10:30a PT sync? Rishi/Laura — can you join to run the MAP?

Thanks,
